sources.dash: Dash 2015 survey for AERA: mean base side 230.363 m; east 230.295-230.373 m, west 230.378-230.436 m (95%)
sources.petrie: Petrie 1883, The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh: base 230.348 m, casing slope 51 deg 52 min +/- 2 min, casing joints mean 0.02 in
sources.cole: Cole 1925, Survey of Egypt Paper 39: sides 230.253 (N) to 230.454 m (S); mean skew about 3 min west of true north
sources.lehner: Lehner 1997, The Complete Pyramids: 280 x 440 royal cubits, seked 5 1/2 palms, platform level within about 2.1 cm (secondary report)
sources.aera_gpmp: AERA Giza Plateau Mapping Project: brass disk on the summit at N 29 58' 44.3830", E 31 07' 57.0194" (Helmert 1906 spheroid)
sources.wgs84: Common WGS84 position of the pyramid's centre: 29.979175 N, 31.134358 E (Wikipedia and mapping services)
sources.si: SI: speed of light 299 792 458 m/s exactly since the 1983 metre; metre first defined in 1791 as 1/10 000 000 of the pole-to-equator quadrant
sources.iau: IAU nominal solar radius 695 700 km; Moon radius 1737.4 km; mean distances 149 597 871 km and 384 400 km; Moon sidereal rotation 27.32 d
sources.trimble: Trimble 1964 and Badawy 1964: King's Chamber shafts at about 45 deg (south) and 32 deg 30 min (north); Gantenbrink 1993: Queen's south shaft about 39 deg 30 min
sources.krupp: Krupp 1997 and later critiques of the Orion correlation (Bauval and Gilbert 1994)
sources.greaves: Greaves, Pyramidographia (1646), from his 1638-39 survey; Newton, A Dissertation upon the Sacred Cubit (published 1737)

claims.title: Base side 756 ft
claims.verdict: 755.78 ft (230.363 m). 756 ft rounds it; the design is 440 royal cubits.

claims.title: Height 480 ft without the capstone, 1/11 mile
claims.claim: Height 480 ft without the capstone, 1/11 mile
claims.verdict: 5280/11 = 480 is true arithmetic. The surveyed apex height is about 481.3 ft (146.7 m). 480 ft 'without the capstone' needs a cap only 0.4 m tall; the pyramidion is lost and its size unknown (Amenemhat III's surviving one is about 1.3 m).

claims.title: Height : base = 7 : 11
claims.verdict: 0.6368 against 0.6364: 280 : 440 royal cubits, the slope of a seked of 5 1/2 palms per cubit.

claims.title: 2.3 million blocks
claims.verdict: An estimate (volume about 2.6 million m3 over an assumed mean block), never a count.

claims.title: Base level to within 15 mm
claims.verdict: Reported deviation of the platform is about 2.1 cm (secondary report of the Cole/Lehner work); Petrie found a 40 ft stretch of the first course level to 0.02 in. Same order of magnitude, not the exact 15 mm.

claims.title: Casing joints under 0.5 mm
claims.verdict: Petrie's mean joint thickness is 1/50 inch (0.51 mm), measured on the few casing stones left at the base.

claims.title: Aligned to true north within 0.1%
claims.verdict: About 3 arcminutes west of north (0.052 deg). '0.1%' is a loose way to say it: as a fraction of a full turn the error is 0.014%.

claims.title: Perimeter / (2 x height) = pi
claims.verdict: 3.1401 +/- 0.0037: pi to 3 significant digits. The seked of 5 1/2 palms makes it 22/7 = 3.1429 by design, so this pi is the builders' 22/7, not the transcendental number.

claims.title: Perimeter / height = tau (2 pi)
claims.verdict: The same ratio as pi, doubled: 6.280. One coincidence, not two.

claims.title: Slant height / half-base = phi
claims.verdict: 1.6195 +/- 0.0012 against 1.6180: phi to 3 significant digits. 14/11 gives 1.6186. pi and phi cannot both be meant exactly: the pi slope is 51.854 deg, the phi slope 51.827 deg, and the survey (51.867 +/- 0.033 deg) cannot tell them apart.

claims.title: Latitude of the Grand Gallery's centre = 29.9792458 N
claims.claim: Latitude of the Grand Gallery's centre = 29.9792458 N
claims.verdict: A 1e-7 degree step is 1.1 cm, so the 230 m pyramid spans about 20800 such latitude lines; one of them must read 29.9792458, and it lies 7.8 m north of the centre, inside the Gallery but 12.5 m south of the Gallery's midpoint (29.979358 N). The building supports 4 to 5 significant digits (29.979). The summit disk on the old Egyptian datum reads 29.978995 N; moved to WGS84 it is 29.979161 N: the datum alone moves the 4th decimal place. The metre is from 1791 and the second's value for c was fixed in 1983.

claims.title: 86 400 seconds in a day
claims.verdict: True by definition: 24 x 60 x 60.

claims.title: Sun's diameter 864 000 miles
claims.verdict: 864 576 miles from the IAU nominal solar radius: 864 000 is 0.07% low.

claims.title: Sun's radius 432 000 miles
claims.verdict: 432 288 miles: 0.07% off. Only in miles: 695 700 km.

claims.title: Moon's radius 1 080 miles
claims.verdict: 1 079.6 miles: 0.04% off. Only in miles: 1 737.4 km.

claims.title: The Sun is 108 Earths wide
claims.verdict: 109.2 (mean Earth radius 6 371 km): 1% off.

claims.title: The Sun is 108 of its own diameters away
claims.claim: The Sun is 108 of its own diameters away
claims.verdict: 107.5 on the mean distance; 105.7 to 109.3 over the year.

claims.title: Meridian 40 000 km
claims.verdict: 40 007.86 km. True because the metre was defined from it in 1791: it says nothing about Giza.

claims.title: Moon 400 times smaller than the Sun
claims.claim: Moon 400 times smaller than the Sun

claims.title: Moon 400 times closer than the Sun
claims.claim: Moon 400 times closer than the Sun
claims.verdict: 389 on mean distances; it swings from about 363 to 425 over the orbits.

claims.title: Earth rotates 400 times faster than the Moon
claims.claim: Earth rotates 400 times faster than the Moon
claims.verdict: 27.4 times faster (sidereal days). No reading gives 400.

claims.title: Greaves surveyed it in 1637
claims.verdict: He was at Giza in 1638-39 and published Pyramidographia in 1646; Newton used his figures for the sacred cubit.

claims.title: Greaves inscribed one English foot in the King's Chamber
claims.claim: Greaves inscribed one English foot in the King's Chamber
claims.verdict: No source found for an inscription; his book prints an English foot so that readers could compare it.

claims.title: King's Chamber shafts: Orion's Belt (south), the pole star Thuban (north)
claims.claim: King's Chamber shafts: Orion's Belt (south), the pole star Thuban (north)
claims.verdict: The shaft angles (about 45 deg and 32.5 deg) meet Alnitak and Thuban around 2500 BC, if the date is chosen to fit; within about 1 deg.

claims.title: Queen's Chamber shafts: Sirius (south), the pole star (north)
claims.claim: Queen's Chamber shafts: Sirius (south), the pole star (north)
claims.verdict: The south shaft (about 39.5 deg) fits Sirius near 2400 BC, but both shafts are closed and bend: they never saw the sky.

claims.title: The three pyramids copy Orion's Belt and point to Heliopolis
claims.claim: The three pyramids copy Orion's Belt and point to Heliopolis
claims.verdict: Contested: the match needs the map turned and the sizes read loosely.
